questions.question: On-premises servers connect to Azure through ExpressRoute private peering. The servers must access a storage account without using the public internet, and public network access to the account must be disabled. What should you configure?

options.text: A private endpoint for the storage account
options.why: Correct. A private endpoint provides a private IP address that on-premises clients can reach over ExpressRoute.

options.text: A service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage on the GatewaySubnet
options.why: Service endpoints do not extend to on-premises clients and require the public endpoint.

options.text: A storage firewall rule that allows the on-premises public IP range
options.why: This uses the public endpoint, which must be disabled.

options.text: A service endpoint policy
options.why: Service endpoint policies restrict service endpoints and do not provide on-premises access.

questions.explanation: Private endpoints are reachable from the virtual network, peered networks and on-premises networks, and allow public network access to be disabled.

questions.question: You create a private endpoint for the blob service of a storage account. VMs in the virtual network still resolve the account name to a public IP address. What should you do?

options.text: Create the privatelink.blob.core.windows.net private DNS zone with a record for the account and link it to the virtual network
options.why: Correct. The private DNS zone resolves the name to the private endpoint IP address.

options.text: Create a second private endpoint for the file service
options.why: A file endpoint does not change name resolution for blob.

options.text: Enable a service endpoint for Microsoft.Storage
options.why: Service endpoints do not change DNS resolution.

options.text: Add a user-defined route to the private endpoint
options.why: Routing does not change the address a name resolves to.

questions.explanation: Private endpoints rely on a privatelink private DNS zone linked to the virtual network. A DNS zone group keeps the A record updated.

questions.question: Only VMs in Subnet1 must be able to access a storage account. Access from on-premises is not required. You want a solution that has no additional cost. What should you configure?

options.text: A Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on Subnet1 and a virtual network rule on the storage account firewall
options.why: Correct. Service endpoints are free and let the storage firewall allow the subnet.

options.text: A private endpoint in Subnet1
options.why: A private endpoint meets the access requirement but is billed per hour and per GB.

options.text: An NSG on Subnet1 that allows the Storage service tag
options.why: An NSG on the subnet does not restrict which networks can reach the storage account.

options.text: A route table that sends Storage traffic to the internet
options.why: This does not restrict access to the storage account.

questions.explanation: Service endpoints identify the subnet to the service so that its firewall can allow only that subnet.

questions.question: You enable a Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on Subnet1. Which next hop type appears in the effective routes of a VM in Subnet1 for the storage address prefixes?

options.text: VirtualNetworkServiceEndpoint
options.why: Correct. Azure adds routes with this next hop type for the service prefixes.

options.text: VirtualAppliance
options.why: This next hop type is used by user-defined routes to an NVA.

options.text: VNetPeering
options.why: This next hop type is used for peered virtual networks.

options.text: VirtualNetworkGateway
options.why: This next hop type is used for routes through a VPN or ExpressRoute gateway.

questions.explanation: Enabling a service endpoint adds system routes for the service prefixes with the next hop type VirtualNetworkServiceEndpoint.

questions.question: Which two statements about private endpoints are true? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: A private endpoint is a network interface that has a private IP address from your subnet.
options.why: Correct. The endpoint is a NIC in your subnet.

options.text: A private endpoint connects to one resource and one target sub-resource, such as blob.
options.why: Correct. Each endpoint maps to a specific sub-resource.

options.text: One private endpoint for a storage account provides access to blob, file, queue and table services.
options.why: You need one endpoint per sub-resource.

options.text: Private endpoints are free.
options.why: Private endpoints are billed per hour and per GB processed.

questions.explanation: Each private endpoint is a NIC that maps to one sub-resource of one resource through Azure Private Link.
